build_specs.task: Build the weekly paid media report (Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn Ads)
inputs: google-ads gaql: last week and the week before, by campaign (ready)
facebook-ads get_insights_adaccount: same weeks, level campaign (ready; read access is enough)
steps: read: pull the three platforms for both weeks
draft: one table per platform (spend, clicks, conversions, cost per conversion, change on the week) and three lines on what moved
write: update_cells into the tab Weekly paid in the marketing ops sheet (approved once at setup by Leo Park)
write: post_message with the three lines and the sheet link to #marketing (approved once at setup by Leo Park)
build_specs.output: the Weekly paid tab and a message in #marketing
build_specs.review_gate: Leo Park reads the message by 10:00 Monday; the channel and the tab were approved once at setup
build_specs.when_it_fails: a failed call posts 'not run: <platform> <action>' and skips both writes; a platform with no spend is shown as no spend, never left out
build_specs.stop_it: delete the Monday schedule; the sheet and channel stay as they are
build_specs.measure: Leo logs minutes for the first four Mondays; working means he changed no number and no conclusion

build_specs.task: Check daily spend pacing on Google Ads, Meta and LinkedIn Ads
inputs: the monthly plan per platform from the team
steps: draft: compare with the plan pro rata to the day, using the pacing band set by Leo Park (plus or minus 10%)
write: post_message to #marketing only when a platform is outside the band (approved once at setup by Leo Park)
build_specs.output: a message in #marketing on the days a platform is off pace; nothing on other days
build_specs.review_gate: Leo Park acts on any message the same day; budget changes stay with him and Dana Whitfield
build_specs.when_it_fails: a failed call posts 'pacing not checked: <platform>' so silence never means on pace by mistake
build_specs.measure: Leo logs minutes for the first four runs; working means no off-pace day was missed

build_specs.task: Write one blog post from the content calendar
build_specs.trigger: Wednesday at 09:00 America/New_York, when the content calendar row for the week is marked Brief ready
inputs: google-sheets query_sheet_data: the week's row in the content calendar (ready)
google-search-console search_analytics: queries for the topic, last 28 days (ready; read access is enough)
steps: read: the brief and the queries
draft: outline, then the full post in the brand voice, with every product claim from the approved list
hand-off: Nina Alvarez edits; Dana Whitfield approves; Nina publishes in WordPress by hand (WordPress isn't connected, so there is no create_post step)
build_specs.output: a draft post for Nina to edit
build_specs.review_gate: Nina edits by Thursday; Dana Whitfield approves before it goes live
build_specs.when_it_fails: no Search Console rows for the topic: the draft says so and works from the brief alone
build_specs.stop_it: stop marking rows Brief ready, or delete the schedule
build_specs.measure: Nina logs minutes for the first four posts, editing included

build_specs.task: Draft and schedule LinkedIn and X posts
build_specs.trigger: Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 08:30 America/New_York
inputs: google-sheets query_sheet_data: the social rows of the content calendar (ready)
steps: draft: the post for LinkedIn or X in the brand voice
write: schedule_linkedin_post or schedule_x_post with status draft (ready), so nothing publishes
hand-off: Nina Alvarez edits the draft and Dana Whitfield approves; Nina sets it to scheduled in the scheduler
build_specs.output: a draft post in the scheduler
build_specs.review_gate: Dana Whitfield approves each post before Nina schedules it
build_specs.when_it_fails: a failed write leaves the draft text in the run report for Nina to paste
build_specs.stop_it: delete the schedule; drafts already in the scheduler stay as drafts
build_specs.measure: Nina logs minutes for the first four posts; the scheduler count per week should stay at 3

build_specs.task: Review Google Ads search terms and add negative keywords
steps: draft: terms that spent with no conversion, grouped by intent, each with its spend; terms that name the service go on a watch list, not the negative list
write: add_negative_keywords with the exact list, only after Dana Whitfield says yes to it (ready: full access)
build_specs.output: a proposed negative list, then the confirmation of what was added
build_specs.review_gate: Dana Whitfield approves the exact list and match types every run
build_specs.when_it_fails: a failed read stops the run; a failed write reports which terms were not added
build_specs.measure: Leo logs minutes for four runs; working means Dana removed no term for being wrong

ai_use_policy.data: Demo request contact details stay in HubSpot. Routing them (T9) stays with Maya Cohen; nobody pastes lead or customer personal data into a prompt.
ai_use_policy.brand_and_claims: Every draft follows the brand voice. Product claims come only from the approved claims list; a new claim goes to Dana Whitfield.
ai_use_policy.disclosure: Follow each platform's rules for labelling AI-made content. Never publish an AI-made review, testimonial or customer quote.

approvals.R1: the owner reads it before sharing (T1, T2, T3)
approvals.R2: Dana Whitfield before a post or blog goes live (T6, T7); customer emails need an approver named (T8)
approvals.R3: Dana Whitfield on the exact change, every run (T4, T5)

ai_use_policy.records: Approvals are logged in the Approvals tab of the marketing ops sheet. Dana Whitfield reviews this policy every quarter (next: 2027-01-28) and after any incident.
ai_use_policy.not_legal_advice: A working policy for the team, not legal advice; health, finance or legal claims need the company's own review.

rollout.pilot_exit: four runs where the reviewer changed no number and no decision; fail that twice and the task goes back to Assist or human
